news.title: Stonebwoy celebrates Black Challenge’s World Cup win after GH¢100,000 backing
news.lede: Stonebwoy has celebrated the Black Challenge’s historic Amputee Football World Cup win, weeks after backing the team with GH¢100,000 ahead of the tournament. Dancehall star Stonebwoy has joined the celebrations over the Black Challenge’s historic triumph at the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup, weeks after backing the team financially ahead of the tournament in Mexico. The Black Challenge beat Morocco 1-0 in the final in San Juan de los Lagos on Sunday, 22 November 2026, to give Ghana its first-ever world title in amputee football. Following the victory, the award-winning musician, born Livingstone Etse Satekla, said he was pleased that his contribution had helped inspire wider support for the team.

news.title: 'I feel ready for it': World Cup wonderkid gives green light to Man Utd transfer
news.lede: Club Brugge wonderkid Joaquin Seys has admitted he is ready for a big transfer to the Premier League next summer after facing interest from the likes of Arsenal and Manchester United. Seys has been thoroughly scouted by a number of Europe’s elite sides after some standout performances for Brugge which also saw him feature for Belgium at the 2026 World Cup. Teams such as United, Arsenal, Aston Villa and Newcastle all reportedly submitted enquiries for Seys in the summer but a deal never materialised, with Brugge thought to be demanding in excess of €30 million for the 21-year-old. However, Seys has insisted he is ‘ready’ to join a big club after starring against the likes of Liverpool, Aston Villa and Inter in the Champions League this season.
